pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all seeded rows are 0 and that 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' asserts exact list [First item, ★ Second item, Third item].
test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1, asserts 200 and ['★ First item','★ Third item'] in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all give the full list in id order.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; the code uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits' (03b1e77, authored by a bot), loosened the 'No starred items' state test. `expect(listed(html)).toEqual([])` became `expect(listed(html)).toBeDefined()`, which can never fail because the array is always defined. The check that the starred view lists nothing is gone. The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', and the spec does not justify the change.
The PR claims no tests were loosened and nothing changed after the go. The final commit weakened an assertion (see the tests finding), so both claims are false.
findings.fix: Revert the loosening, or disclose it in the PR body.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's two decisions: starred items keep their id order, and the view is a query parameter with no cookie. It adds no behaviour beyond the spec, apart from the traffic-check regex relaxation that AC-7 requires.
All 7 acceptance items are implemented. All 4 state-table rows have tests, but the 'No starred items' test was weakened (see findings).

The tests were not run here; CI runs them via scripts/check-fast.sh. One assertion in the 'No starred items' test can never fail (finding). The traffic fake app and traffic-config tests were extended.
The README mentions ?show=starred. It does not mention the ★ marker, which is minor.
The view is selected with Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is safely rejected. SQL is built only from fixed view strings. No defects found.
The show parameter is allow-listed. Titles are HTML-escaped. No instructions planted in the repo content.
The diff adds only a minimal server-rendered HTML link and list. There are no CSS or UI component files.
There are no UI component or browser flows in the diff. The server-rendered HTML is covered by the Worker tests.
The 'tests loosened: none' and 'changed after the go: nothing' claims are false (finding). The other claims match the diff.
